depth.h2: What McHenry Homes Need From a Plumber
depth.intro: The median home in McHenry was built in 1988, and about 3 in 4 went up between 1970 and 2009. Add hard groundwater, the Fox River and long McHenry County winters, and the same few problems keep showing up.

tiles.title: Groundwater and Your Water Heater
tiles.body: McHenry County gets its water from underground aquifers, not Lake Michigan. Groundwater here tends to be hard, and in some areas it carries iron that stains fixtures orange and leaves sediment in the bottom of water heaters. That buildup makes a water heater work harder and wear out sooner. [Flushing and servicing your water heater](/mchenry/water-heater-repair) helps, and a [water filtration system](/mchenry/water-filtration-systems) can cut down on buildup.

tiles.title: The Fox River and Wet Basements
tiles.body: In July 2017, heavy rain flooded the Fox River and the Chain O’Lakes, McHenry County was declared a state disaster area, and homes along the river and the lakes took on water. You don’t have to live on the river to get a wet basement, though. A [sump pump with a battery backup](/mchenry/sump-pumps) keeps running when the power goes out, and a [backflow valve](/mchenry/flood-control-maintenance) stops sewage from coming up through floor drains.

tiles.title: Homes From the 1990s and 2000s
tiles.body: About 4 in 10 McHenry homes went up between 1990 and 2009. Equipment that came with the house, like the first water heater and the first sump pump, isn’t built to last as long as the house. If yours has never been replaced, a [whole-home checkup](/mchenry/plumbing-maintenance) tells you what’s close to the end before it fails.

tiles.title: Hard Freezes and Hidden Leaks
tiles.body: McHenry County winters bring long stretches below freezing. Pipes in exterior walls, crawl spaces and outdoor spigot lines freeze first, and a split pipe often starts leaking inside a wall or under a floor once it thaws. We can [find and fix the leak](/mchenry/leak-repairs), and we’re on call 24/7 if a [pipe bursts](/mchenry/burst-pipe-repair).

items.q: Is McHenry’s hard water tough on my water heater?
items.preview: It can be. Groundwater in McHenry County tends to be hard, and some areas also have iron.
items.a: It can be. Groundwater in McHenry County tends to be hard, and some areas also have iron. Those minerals settle in your water heater as sediment, which makes it work harder and wear out sooner. Signs include a popping or rumbling tank, rusty hot water and hot water that runs out faster than it used to. Flushing your water heater regularly helps, and a [water filtration system](/mchenry/water-filtration-systems) can cut down on buildup.

items.q: When should I replace my water heater?
items.preview: With hard water, sooner rather than later.
items.a: With hard water, sooner rather than later. Tank water heaters usually last somewhere around 8 to 12 years. Rusty water, rumbling noises, a leak at the base or hot water that runs out faster than it used to all mean it’s time to have it checked. [Replacing it](/mchenry/water-heater-installation) on your schedule is easier than dealing with a flooded basement.

items.q: Why are there orange stains in my sinks and tub?
items.preview: Orange or rust-colored stains usually come from iron in the water.
items.a: Orange or rust-colored stains usually come from iron in the water. It isn’t a health hazard, but it stains fixtures and laundry, and the same iron settles as sediment in your water heater and pipes. A [water test](/mchenry/water-filtration-systems) shows what’s in your water, so you know whether filtration makes sense for your home.

items.q: How do I protect my basement from sewer backups?
items.preview: Start with three things: a backflow valve on your sewer line, a sump pump with a battery backup, and a regular check of your sewer line for roots and debris.
items.a: Start with three things: a backflow valve on your sewer line, a sump pump with a battery backup, and a regular check of your sewer line for roots and debris. For homes with repeat backups, an [overhead sewer system](/mchenry/overhead-sewer-systems) lifts basement wastewater above the level where backups happen. We can look at your setup and tell you which option makes sense for your home.
